about: Golden vectors for the Invariant compiled-program IR. Any engine claiming to run this IR must produce these outputs, including the refusals. A refusal is part of the contract: an engine that rounds where this one rejects is not compatible.

vectors.name: move renames a field
vectors.why: The simplest op, and the one every other case is built on.

vectors.name: move into a nested object creates the parent
vectors.why: Unnesting and nesting are the same op, so the target may not exist.

vectors.name: move out of a nested object prunes the empty parent
vectors.why: Leaving `payment_method: {}` behind would not match the old contract.

vectors.name: move does nothing when the field is absent
vectors.why: An optional field a caller did not send must not appear as null.

vectors.name: scale moves the decimal point right
vectors.why: Multiplying by a hundred is wrong: 19.99 * 100 is 1998.9999999999998.

vectors.name: scale moves the decimal point left
vectors.why: The inverse has to be exact too, or a round trip loses money.

vectors.name: scale refuses a value it cannot represent exactly
vectors.why: Three decimal places scaled by two leaves a fraction of a minor unit. Rounding here would be silent data loss in money, so it refuses.

vectors.name: scale keeps a large integer exact
vectors.why: A value beyond double precision must not be rounded on the way through.

vectors.name: enum maps a known value
vectors.why: The ordinary vocabulary change.

vectors.name: enum refuses a value it has no mapping for
vectors.why: Passing an unmapped value through would hand the caller a word its contract never defined, and it would look like a success.

vectors.name: a lenient enum passes an unmapped value through
vectors.why: Only for a field naming another field, such as an error's `param`. An unfamiliar name there is harmless; failing the response is not.

vectors.name: set fills a field the caller omitted
vectors.why: A caller written before a required field existed never sends one.

vectors.name: set leaves a value the caller did supply
vectors.why: A default must never overwrite an explicit choice.

vectors.name: del removes a field
vectors.why: The old contract never had it, so it must not be in the response.

vectors.name: set with ifNull fills a null and nothing else
vectors.why: A response field that became nullable is shown to an old caller with the value the provider chose, and never created where it was absent.

vectors.name: set with ifAbsent and ifNull fills either
vectors.why: A response field that became optional and nullable is always there, and never null, for an old caller.

vectors.name: del with ifNull drops a null and nothing else
vectors.why: A request field that no longer accepts null is left out when an old caller sends null, where the new contract lets it be absent.

vectors.name: del with ifNull leaves a value
vectors.why: Only the null the new contract refuses is dropped.

vectors.name: a wildcard applies to every element of a list
vectors.why: A list envelope is the common shape and the one with a fan-out cost.

vectors.name: a wildcard over an empty list does nothing
vectors.why: No elements is not an error, and must not be one.

vectors.name: a wildcard move creates the target in each element
vectors.why: Creating a slot per element is where a naive implementation goes wrong.

vectors.name: cast turns a number into a string
vectors.why: Some contracts carry identifiers as one and some as the other.

vectors.name: instructions apply in order
vectors.why: A rename followed by a conversion targets the new name. Applying them in any other order finds nothing and silently does half the work.

vectors.name: a wildcard at the cap transforms every element
vectors.why: The cap is a ceiling, not a sample: a body within it is transformed whole.

vectors.name: a wildcard past the cap at the end of a path is refused
vectors.why: Transforming the first N elements and leaving the rest is a body in the wrong shape that nothing reports. It is refused whole instead.

vectors.name: a wildcard past the cap in the middle of a path is refused
vectors.why: Dropping every match here would skip the instruction entirely, which is the same silent wrong shape. It is refused whole instead.

vectors.name: within runs a block at every element of a list
vectors.why: A Change to one element of a list is written once, relative to the element.

vectors.name: switch runs only the block for the variant the key names
vectors.why: A Change to one variant of a union must not touch the others, which may have a field of the same name meaning something else.

vectors.name: switch reads its key once, before the block can change it
vectors.why: Which variant a value is must not depend on what the block does to it.

vectors.name: switch on a number or a boolean matches its text
vectors.why: A discriminator is not always a string.

vectors.name: has runs its block only where the field is present
vectors.why: A union told apart by which field it has, rather than by a key's value.

vectors.name: has with absent runs its block only where a field is missing
vectors.why: Stripe's live and deleted objects share their type and differ only in that the deleted one carries `deleted`; the live one is known by its absence.

vectors.name: an object a within reached becomes its own id
vectors.why: A union gained a kind of object old callers never heard of. Stripe sends the id of an object a caller did not expand, and the old union allows it.

vectors.name: list items a within reached are removed, however many
vectors.why: Removing an item shifts the ones after it. Every one chosen has to go, and no other, whatever order they were found in.

vectors.name: a value a within reached is replaced with null
vectors.why: Where old callers could be sent null, a value they cannot read becomes one.

vectors.name: an instruction that would replace a whole body is refused
vectors.why: Only a value inside a body can be replaced; a body is what the caller sent.

vectors.name: a key read through a wildcard is refused
vectors.why: A key is one value at one place; a wildcard would make it several.

vectors.name: blocks nested past the limit are refused
vectors.why: Each level multiplies how many places one instruction reaches.

vectors.name: a program naming a prototype key is refused
vectors.why: `__proto__` reaches an object every other object shares. A program is data from a build, and a build can be wrong; this must not be reachable.

vectors.name: call runs a named block where it stands
vectors.why: A block shared by every place a schema sits runs as if written at the call.

vectors.name: a block calls itself to follow a tree to its leaves
vectors.why: A schema that contains itself has no last place to list. The block descends and calls itself, so every level is translated, however deep.

vectors.name: is runs its block only where a value is of one kind
vectors.why: Stripe's expandable fields hold an id or the whole object. Only the object has fields to translate; the id passes untouched.

vectors.name: is tells a number however it was written
vectors.why: A number is a number whether or not it is kept as its exact digits.

vectors.name: a call to a block the contract does not have is refused
vectors.why: A program naming instructions it does not carry cannot be run as written.

vectors.name: blocks that call one another without descending are refused
vectors.why: A call runs where it stands, so a cycle that never moves into the value would never end. Only recursion that follows the value is allowed.

envelopes.name: a query parameter is renamed
envelopes.why: The commonest parameter break, and the case every other one builds on.

envelopes.name: an untouched query parameter keeps its exact bytes and its place
envelopes.why: Re-encoding what no Change named would break a signature or a cache key that depends on those bytes, for no reason at all.

envelopes.name: a parameter the caller did not send stays unsent
envelopes.why: An optional parameter must not appear because a Change named it.

envelopes.name: a query number is scaled exactly
envelopes.why: Parameters are typed from their declaration, so a scale sees a number.

envelopes.name: a query value that is not a number is refused by the scale that needs one
envelopes.why: Text a number was declared for is passed to the instruction as text, which refuses it.

envelopes.name: a query value is mapped
envelopes.why: An enum rename on a parameter is the same instruction as on a field.

envelopes.name: a newly required query parameter is supplied
envelopes.why: A default an old caller never sent, added without overwriting one they did.

envelopes.name: a repeated query parameter becomes a comma-separated one
envelopes.why: The value is a list either way; only how the contract writes it changed.

envelopes.name: a header is renamed whatever case the caller wrote it in
envelopes.why: Header names are case-insensitive, so matching one exactly would miss it.

envelopes.name: a query parameter moves into a header
envelopes.why: Moving between locations is one move in one tree.

envelopes.name: a query parameter moves into the body
envelopes.why: A search that moves from the query string into a JSON body is a location move like any other, and the body is read only because a program reaches it.

envelopes.name: a path parameter is mapped and written back into the path
envelopes.why: A path parameter can be converted in place; the template is unchanged.

envelopes.name: a path parameter can only be converted
envelopes.why: A template has the parameters it has, so moving one out is refused at load.

envelopes.name: a cookie is renamed and the others are kept
envelopes.why: Cookies are addressed one by one; the rest of the header is not the program's.

envelopes.name: a deepObject is renamed, and a prototype key in it is dropped
envelopes.why: Property names in a deepObject are the caller's to choose, `__proto__` included, and it must never become a key of anything.

envelopes.name: a header value that would break the line is refused
envelopes.why: A line break in a header value is how a request is smuggled.

envelopes.name: a program touching a credential header is refused
envelopes.why: A program that can move a credential can move it somewhere it is logged.

envelopes.name: a program naming a parameter it does not declare is refused
envelopes.why: Every parameter a program rewrites has to say how it is written.

envelopes.name: a program addressing every query parameter at once is refused
envelopes.why: A wildcard over the query string would rewrite parameters nobody declared.

forms.name: a nested field is renamed in bracketed keys
forms.why: Stripe writes nested fields as `metadata[order]=`, and a rename inside one is the commonest nested change.

forms.name: a pair no instruction names keeps its exact bytes
forms.why: Re-encoding what no Change named would change bytes someone may depend on, for no reason.

forms.name: a field in every element of a list is renamed
forms.why: Stripe writes lists of objects as `items[0][price]=`, and the wildcard has to reach each one.

forms.name: a repeated plain field is renamed and stays repeated
forms.why: Twilio writes a list as the same key repeated, with no brackets.

forms.name: a plain field's value is mapped
forms.why: An enum rename is the same instruction in a form as in JSON.

forms.name: a newly required field is supplied
forms.why: A default an old caller never sent, without overwriting one they did.

forms.name: a null is written as an empty value
forms.why: An empty value is how a form says unset, which is what Stripe reads it as.

forms.name: a prototype key inside a bracketed field is dropped
forms.why: Keys inside brackets are the caller's to choose, and `__proto__` must never become one.

forms.name: a value a number was declared for, written as text, is refused by the scale
forms.why: The form carries text; typing it is what lets a scale refuse what is not a number.

forms.name: a declaration naming a prototype key is refused
forms.why: A program is data from a build, and a build can be wrong.
